# Sourdough Baking Guide

A reliable weekend sourdough loaf needs only flour, water, salt, and an active starter.

## Feeding the starter

Feed your starter every twelve hours when kept at room temperature. Discard all but fifty grams, then add fifty grams of flour and fifty grams of water. A healthy starter doubles in size within six hours and smells pleasantly sour, like yogurt. If you bake less often, store the starter in the refrigerator and feed it once a week.

## Mixing and bulk fermentation

Mix 500 grams of bread flour with 350 grams of water and let it rest for thirty minutes. This rest is called the autolyse. Add 100 grams of active starter and 10 grams of salt, then fold the dough every thirty minutes for the first two hours. Bulk fermentation takes about five hours at 24 degrees Celsius. The dough is ready when it has grown by half and feels airy.

## Shaping and proofing

Shape the dough into a tight round and place it seam side up in a floured banneton. For the best flavor, proof the shaped loaf in the refrigerator overnight for twelve to sixteen hours.

## Baking

Preheat a Dutch oven at 250 degrees Celsius for forty-five minutes. Score the loaf with a razor blade, bake covered for twenty minutes, then uncover and bake for another twenty-five minutes at 220 degrees until the crust is deep brown. Cool the loaf on a wire rack for at least one hour before slicing.

## Common problems

A dense crumb usually means the dough was under-fermented. A flat loaf often means the dough was over-proofed. If the crust is pale, bake it a few minutes longer with the lid off.
